newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tower in EPROM pact with Fairchild.
newsitem.headline: Tower in EPROM pact with Fairchild.

text.p: Israel's Tower Semiconductor Ltd and Fairchild Semiconductor Corp of the United States said on Sunday they had reached a long-term agreement to produce and market EPROM chips.

Under the agreement, Fairchild will provide product definition, package, test and market the low-voltage, high density Erasable Programmable Read Only Memories. Tower, a semiconductor foundry, will fabricate the wafers.

Reuven Marko, Tower's director of marketing and sales, told Reuters the agreement would enable the compamy to enter a new field. He said, however, it would be difficult to place a value on the agreement with Fairchild.
Tower said its target was to begin producing the EPROMs in large volumes in the second half of the year.

"In combination with the advanced architecture we use, Tower's silicon will help us deliver the smallest, most cost effective die in the world, density for density," Howard Shumway, Fairchild's EPROM product director, said in a statement.

Fairchild Semiconductor was spun off earlier this year from National Semiconductor Corp, which has a long-term realtionship with Tower. But Marko said the Fairchild agreement was separate and represented a new business. - Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
